title: Redo role-prompt goal-preservation change; update every 1,800 mention
summary: Redo job 20261014-170031-2r9b from the base. Edit the reader, producer and verifier prompts so the request's real goal survives to the verdict. Make a non-empty request_reading_mismatch a Major finding in judge(), raise the reader budget only as far as needed, and update every document that states the old 1,800 budget. The earlier failure was two missed present-tense mentions (defaults-loop.md:47 and socratic-review.md:219).

defaults_applied.how: Grep every statement of the reader budget so none is missed, which was the prior failure.
New judge() unit tests; budgets, fmt, clippy and tests must pass.
Decision record and changelog written for an outside reader.
The new budget is the measured token count from the budgets test.
The retry scope is recovered from the earlier job's reading and verifier findings.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audience for this change is the maintainers who run Athena jobs and the three role agents reading these prompts.
The retry starts from base, so all of the earlier work is redone, and the two missed budget mentions are fixed.
Past-tense measurements in review documents are history and may keep 1,800.
The new request's advice to give evidence per criterion is met by the producer checking each criterion against the diff and tests before finishing; no code change is needed for it.

acceptance_criteria.text: reader.md tells the reader to name the request's audience (who will use or judge the result) in the summary or assumptions.
reader.md requires at least one acceptance criterion written as an outcome the named audience can check; presence checks alone do not satisfy it.
reader.md forbids putting the request's own stated goal in out_of_scope, and tells the reader to read the current output the request is about before planning a change to it.
producer.md treats the acceptance criteria as a floor and tells the producer to serve the request's goal, while keeping the small-change and follow-conventions instructions.
verifier.md tells the verifier to judge user-facing output as its intended audience would, and to rate a request-reading mismatch at least major, never minor because the criteria passed.

In judge() in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, a non-empty request_reading_mismatch adds a Major finding and a reason, so the verdict is not pass. Unit tests cover mismatch present and absent or blank. Run: cargo test -p athena-core verify
The BudgetSet::Reader budget is raised only as far as the new reader text needs. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets
docs/decisions.md records the new reader budget, the measured count and why removals cannot pay for the new rules; CHANGELOG.md notes the change.

No present-tense statement of the old 1,800 reader budget remains in the docs. Specifically update defaults-loop.md:47, :227 and :413, decision-sets.md:107 and :111, decisions.md:612, athena-v0.md:1507 and :1868, and socratic-review.md:219 (and :198 if present tense). Past-tense review and history records may keep 1,800. Keep wrapped lines near the file's width.
The workspace stays clean and tested. Run: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test

out_of_scope: Adding a repair loop or changing the job lifecycle (the introspection's design-change suggestion)
Editing historical review documents that record past measurements
Changing any budget other than the reader's
departures: The cost and time medians are slightly above the reference, because the change spans three prompts, Rust code with tests, and many documents, and the previous attempt failed on a missed doc.
